text:
The firm's stored knowledge doesn't mention Joad, so I can't say what Joad requires before agreeing to anything about its test records or what limits apply to its settlement offers. Joad isn't the client (Toil & Trouble Home Products), and nothing in the client or firm stores identifies Joad's role, its test-record requirements, or its settlement constraints. I'd rather not guess. If Joad is a co-party, retailer, insurer, or opposing party, those terms would have to come from a document or instruction I don't have, such as a protective order, an agreement, or Joad's own correspondence.

The stores do cover related points on the Toil & Trouble side:

- **Settlement limits:** The firm has no settlement authority unless it is given. No offer may be made in any form without written approval from General Counsel Franklin Oyelaran. Communications go to him, copied to Delphine Moorcroft in risk management.
- **Approval tiers:** Before any number is communicated, even as a signal, confirm in writing who must approve it and at what level (general counsel, CFO, board, or insurer). Don't rely on verbal indications. Offers above the insurer or officer tier can take weeks to approve, so flag that early.
- **Test and product records:** Nothing may be disassembled or cleaned before both sides' engineers are present, and the client's engineer handles the product only in counsel's presence. Don't volunteer complaint history or other incidents until a request is served and scope has been discussed. Quality records are available from Rennick Odell on request.

If you can tell me who Joad is or send the document that sets out its position, I can answer directly.
